title: Champagne news-letters to the duc de Nevers, June 1590 (BnF fr. 3623 nos. 24, 25, 60; no. 78 of 1591 listed; catalogue item 30)

plaintext.source: a few letters glossed over figures in nos. 25 and 60, and (found by Andrew Beling, 11 Nov 2026) over both runs of no. 24

transcription.notes: Ten runs in one hand and five single figures in no. 24; interlinear glosses faint. Corrected 12 Nov 2026 from Beling's check on the image (PR #422): no. 24 l. 8 fifth figure 56 (36 or 56 on the image), l. 22 '99 9b 56 93 35' (barred 9, then 56), the barred 22, 51, 44, the plain 84, and a barred 17 in line 20 seen at the integration check. A trailing b marks an overbar.
One group of mixed figures and signs; a different mixed code from the two-digit alphabet of nos. 24/25/60 (NOTES), listed here unread with no claim that it shares a key.

system.summary: A two-digit homophonic alphabet whose values rise with the alphabet (a in the 30s, e in the 40s, n in the 60s, u in the 90s), with plain nulls and overbarred figures for names: Nevers key no. 25 (BnF fr. 3995 f. 51r).
system.sibling_key: Nevers key no. 25 (BnF fr. 3995 f. 51r, Oct 1589), matched by Michael Brackx; Tomokiyo's Nevers key no. 46 and Lauriere's key no. 57 tried and do not fit; siblings nos. 26/27 in another key
system.notes: No. 78's single group of mixed figures and signs is another code, unread. Split 14 Oct 2026: no. 23 (name code with its own key slip) is bienvenut1590; Lauriere's 1593 letters in Nevers key no. 57 are lauriere1593.

prior_solution.where: a few interlinear glosses over single figures in nos. 24, 25 and 60 (those of no. 24 found on 11 Nov 2026)

conditions.human_role: Project-level: set up Claude Code and posed the catalogue task via a parent agent. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Tomokiyo's nevers.htm and GL.htm, DECODE list for fr. 3623/3625; no prior reading; DECODE gives folios.
Gallica thumbnails of both volumes; contact sheets; full-resolution pages of ff. 35-41, 88, 111 (fr. 3623) and ff. 10, 16 (fr. 3625).
Tomokiyo's no. 46 (targets/nevers1593/key46.txt) tried on no. 24's figures: values do not fit.
Twelve two-digit runs of nos. 24, 25, 60 transcribed with the faint interlinear letters.
Interlinear glosses (Ludovic, union, a, n) give anchors; the values rise with the alphabet.
Alphabetical slots fill the table: la ligue, de la defiance du [17], de Chazeron, service read; two no. 24 runs stay open.
Key no. 57 tried on no. 78's single group '96 □ 3 9̄ f 3': no sense.

Key no. 57 (words57.tsv and the row + 14 x vowel syllables) applied to the two-digit runs of nos. 24/25/60: no sense ('qui pi bo ni lo fi ...'), confirming a different system; those 41 open figures stay without key.

Nos. 24/25/60: unknown letter values bracketed between known neighbours by the alphabetical order (52 h-i, 62 l-n, 92 s-v, 94 u-v, 95 u-z), all 240 combinations scored with fr-1600-letters over the ten runs, codes left out (anneal_twodigit.py). Best 52 i, 62 n, 92 u/v, 95 y ('de Launan', '...audovic'); none verifies on a second occurrence (92's second occurrence gives 'le [99] y u a v [05] i s'). Not accepted; 63/104 unchanged.

Entry split under the one-key rule (Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): no. 23 (Bienvenut, name code with its key slip f. 36r) moved to bienvenut1590, and Lauriere's letters in Nevers key no. 57 (fr. 3625 nos. 55 and 10, fr. 3985 f. 58) to lauriere1593. This entry keeps the two-digit alphabet of nos. 24/25/60, with no. 78 listed unread; fraction recomputed on its documents: 63 of 110 tokens.
Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 83 tokens, 28 types, fr-1600-letters order 4: reading -2.075 per letter; Verdict: too short.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): transcriptions ct_3623_twodigit.txt and ct_3623_78.txt; readings table, no. 78 note and the two-digit alphabet copied verbatim from NOTES.md into texts/ (n24-25-60_decryption.md, n78_decryption.md, key.md). No. 78 has no decryption (unread).

Method restored: key obtained by the letters glossed over single figures in fr. 3623 nos. 25 and 60 (key recovered based on adjacent plaintext); text not read, class stays not read. The 22-24 Oct reading audit had set the method to not solved because the class was not read; George Lasry (24 Oct 2026) separates the two.

Brackx compared Nevers keys on their photographs following Tomokiyo's catalogue: key no. 25 (fr. 3995 f. 51r, Oct 1589) has the alphabet fingerprint (37 c, 38 d, 47 g, 53/54 i, 56 l, 63/64 n, 67 o, 93 u); keys 28, 30, 38 do not. Its null list and barred entries give plain 39 null, barred 39 La Noue, barred 17 Soissons.
Brackx transcribed the whole recto of no. 25 and read it with key no. 25: 63 of 64 cipher groups (one isolated 3 unread; one 58 -> 56 correction); French reading and English.

Taken in here: key no. 25's letter values checked against the alphabet bracketed from the glosses (all agree); Tomokiyo's catalogue entry for no. 25 confirmed in research/gallica_siblings/src/nevers.htm; no. 25 reading measured 0.925 (v10). Key sheet image not re-checked (Gallica bot check).

Beling: no. 24's two cipher runs found to carry contemporary interlinear letters, unused so far. Check, pre-registered by the contributor's record (the pull request is one commit), (beling/PREREG.md) of key no. 25 unchanged on the 14 legible glossed figures: 13 agree (0.929); 200 shuffled keys mean 0.053, best 0.357; margin 0.571. Pass, small sample.

Beling: key no. 25 sheet (fr. 3995 f. 51r) transcribed: names 1-51, words x-lvii, cities lviii-89, provinces a-z (beling/transcription/key25_*.tsv). Barred 22, 44, 51 in no. 24 confirmed as Guise, La Chastre, La Guiche; 84 not barred (plain s); l. 22 figures read 99 9b 56 93 35 (barred 9 = Roy); 'xlm' in l. 11 read xliij = 43 Intelligence.

Beling: clear text of no. 24 (50 lines, about 15 doubtful words) and no. 60 (5 lines) transcribed and read with the runs (beling/results/n24_reading.md). No. 60's gloss over 64 is a dotted y: 'Launay'. Read share not measured.

Beling: second transcription of no. 25, hashed before Brackx's was opened (not fully blind). Of Brackx's 37 doubtful words, 14 agree, 13 read otherwise, 10 doubtful for both; about 18 other differences. The l. 34 run may end 38 93 9b 'du [Roy]', not B:39 La Noue; 'l'union' has 58 on the page, so 58->56 is an emendation (beling/results/n25_compare.md).

Integration of PR #422 after an independent verification. Reproduced: the ten frozen hashes; 13 of 14 glossed figures of no. 24 agree with key no. 25 (0.929; 200 shuffled keys mean 0.053, best 0.357; a wider control of 3 x 2,000 shuffles, best 0.357 to 0.429); a second parser and scorer give the same 13 of 14; runs_mechanical.txt identical. Two of the 14 are not independent of the figure correction: the glosses l and u sit over the figures Beling re-read (95 93 to barred 9, 56, 93), though the image supports him. On the Gallica images (openapi.bnf.fr IIIF) the run figures agree 25 of 25 in no. 24 and 17 of 17 in no. 60. No. 25 l. 34: the verifier's look agrees with Beling (38 93 and a barred 9, 'du [Roy]') against Brackx's barred 39 ('du M. de La Noue'); both readings are kept and Brackx is to be asked. Not checked: the key sheet names and cities, the clear text beyond the run lines, the 30-odd word differences in no. 25. Done here: ct_3623_twodigit.txt corrected (110 tokens, 43 distinct); texts entries for nos. 24 and 60 with English translations written from Beling's French; both read as sentences; read shares measured with research/reading_audit/v10_relabel.py: no. 24 0.957 (761 words, 34 holes), no. 60 0.938 (45 words, 3 holes); the verifier's count without the bracketed abbreviation expansions is about 0.98 and 0.956. In no. 24 line 20 the figure 17 carries an overbar on the image (one look here): set as barred 17, comte de Soissons, where Beling has the number 17.

Bracketed abbreviation expansions, doubtful and supplied words all count as holes. No. 78 (one unread group in another code) is not in the figure.
outcome.notes: No. 25 read in part with Nevers key no. 25 (Brackx, issue #96), with a second reader (Beling) who differs in about 30 places, among them the end of the l. 34 run (Roy or La Noue); nos. 24 and 60 transcribed and deciphered by one reader (Beling, PR #422); no. 78 unread. texts.label: No. 25, f. 38r, 5 Jun 1590 (DECODE R9455)
texts.summary: An unsigned newsletter to the duc de Nevers from the royal army, 5 June 1590: Paris pressed by famine and division, the legate and the Spanish ambassador at the end of their resources, the Pope awaiting the Holy Spirit, Mayenne gathering weak forces, Villeroy working for peace in vain; in cipher, the union, Chaseron's affairs, the League, and the comte de Soissons's distrust, of M. de La Noue in Michael Brackx's reading shown here, of the King in Andrew Beling's second reading.
texts.note: 25 Oct 2026: Brackx's reading with Nevers key no. 25; 0.925 of words read as sense (v10); one cipher figure unread. 11 Nov 2026: a second reader (Beling, beling/transcription/n25_second_reading.md, compared in beling/results/n25_compare.md) differs in about 30 places; the text shown is Brackx's, unchanged. At l. 34 Beling reads 38 93 and a barred 9, 'du [Roy]', where Brackx has barred 39, 'du M. de La Noue'; the independent verifier's look at the image agrees with Beling. Beling's other alternatives, one reader each: 'elle demeura a Gonnesse' for 'd'ille derechef a Compiegne', 'd'Auvergne' for 'd'Arques', 'a la puissance' for 'a la misericorde'. The page has 58 in 'l'union'; 56 is an emendation of the encipherer.

reading_review.note: Read as French prose: paragraphs C, D, E and J run as coherent sentences (the Pope and the Holy Spirit, Mayenne gathering forces, the primate of Lyon refused a passport, Mayenne to his sister); the cipher runs fit their clear context (the edict of union, Chaseron, la ligue at Arques, Soissons and La Noue). Breaks in A (poix/doigt), B (Lamour, ruine), F (the words after service), H (balliages de flandre), I (Breda, Maure) and K (the besieged town), all marked as holes. 62% of sentences clean on _check_reading; read_share 0.925.

texts.label: No. 24, f. 37r, 15 Jun 1590 (DECODE R9454)
texts.summary: An unsigned newsletter to the duc de Nevers from the royal camp before Paris, 11 to 15 June 1590: little hope of peace; copies wanted by Nevers obtainable only through La Guiche, ill at Compiegne; the King's night march against Saint-Paul at Meaux; a commission refused as burdensome at Senlis; the bread of the poor in Paris; La Chastre said to be worked on through Madame la princesse and Beauvais-Nangis; four soldiers who seized the keep of Vincennes hanged; the army's quarters around Paris on the 14th; Richelieu dead and his office of grand provost given to Fontenay; Brigard refused a passport to Mayenne; Mayenne's siege of Crecy-en-Laonnois raised. In cipher: Guise, La Guiche, 'de Ludouic', 'intelligences', 'le Roy luy avoit', La Chastre.
texts.note: 11 Nov 2026: transcribed and deciphered with Nevers key no. 25 by Andrew Beling (PR #422), one reader, a first pass. 12 Nov 2026: English translation written at the integration check; read share 0.957 by v10_relabel (761 words, 34 holes: 15 doubtful places, one unread passage, the bracketed expansions); without the expansions about 0.98 (the verifier's count). The run figures were confirmed on the image at the verification; the clear text beyond the run lines was not. In line 20 the barred 17 (comte de Soissons) is the integration check's single look; Beling has the number 17.

reading_review.by: project (integration check of PR #422), after the contributor's own reader
reading_review.note: Read end to end as French sentences and translated sentence by sentence: a coherent camp newsletter whose items follow one another (the despatch of the 7th, the King's march of the 11th, Saint-Paul in Brie, Vincennes, the quarters of the 14th, Richelieu's office, Brigard, Crecy). The cipher runs fit their clear context. Weak places, all marked: line 7 ([?Sire]), lines 10-12 (the powder, [?Chauny], the margin sign), line 45 ([?l'an]), line 48 (an unread passage before 'deux pieces de canon'). One reader's transcription; no second reader of the clear text.

texts.label: No. 60, f. 88r, slip of 7 Jun 1590 (DECODE R9459)
texts.summary: A slip of five lines to the duc de Nevers: what the writer wrote about the sieur Ludouic is true; having seen the extract of Nevers's letters, someone confirmed it to him, and will also say how it stands with Launan (the decipherer of the time wrote Launay). Both names are in cipher; neither person is identified.
texts.note: 11 Nov 2026: transcribed and deciphered by Andrew Beling (PR #422), one reader. Read share 0.938 by v10_relabel (45 words, 3 holes), under the 95% bar; about 0.956 without the bracketed expansion. A possible 'au s[ieu]r de Launay' before the second run is one look by the verifier and is recorded as a candidate in the reading file.

reading_review.by: project (integration check of PR #422), after the contributor's own reader
reading_review.note: Two sentences, both coherent; two doubtful words ([?il], [?s']) and the name Launan/Launay open.
